messages:
sarah: Quick heads-up — Finance flagged a ~22% higher committed-unit GPU cost for ap-southeast1 vs us-east1 in Feb. Raw list GPU price is lower in APAC, but invoice shows higher effective cost after line items. Anyone seen this pattern or have pointers? @finance-bot
finance-bot: Billing anomaly detected for account rwd-prod. Variance: ap-southeast1 +21.7% vs us-east1. Possible causes: inter-region egress, sustained-use discounts not applied, committed SKUs mismatch. See: https://billing.redwood/internal/variance/1865432100

mike: I pulled the billing CSV and ran a quick pivot. Two things jump out: 1) we have cross-region snapshot replication traffic from APAC clusters to US backup during night windows — that egress is billed to ap-southeast1. 2) our reserved commitment SKU in APAC is a 1yr partial upfront with different effective hourly rate due to conversion.

janet: Really useful. Are the APAC clusters on Private or Dedicated? If Private, egress to our backup region might be on customer VPC interconnects which are billed differently.

sarah: Dedicated pools in ap-southeast1 and us-east1. Backups use cross-region block replication to us-east1 during daily snapshot dumps.

mike: Here's a tiny snippet of calc I used: 
```
# effective unit cost = (compute_cost + egress_cost + storage_snapshot_cost) / GPU_hours
us-east1: (12000 + 300) / 1000 = $12.30/hr equivalent
ap-southeast1: (9000 + 1800 + 400) / 900 = $12.95/hr equivalent
# APAC cheaper on compute but egress+snapshot pushes it up
```

diego: Oof. That replication schedule is our old default. We moved to global backups but didn't update the APAC routing after Dedicated rollout. We can: 1) change snapshot target to regional object store, 2) move commit consumption to spot for batch, or 3) renegotiate commit SKU with provider in APAC.

ali: Also check network egress tiers — some clouds charge higher egress on particular peering links. I saw a similar delta last quarter where peering -> backbone added 0.02 USD/GB. Multiply by nightly snapshot GBs and it adds up.

janet: From capacity planning POV: if APAC effective cost stays higher, we should prioritize latency-sensitive inference in APAC (to avoid cross-region egress) but move batch-heavy/throughput traffic to us-east1 where cost-per-token is lower after accounting for egress.

mike: Agreed. Quick proposal:
- Stop cross-region snapshot replication for Dedicated pools in APAC (switch to regional snapshots).
- Replace 50% of APAC committed hours for batch queues with reserved spot-backed pools (policy: preemptible accepted).
- Finance to validate whether committed SKU conversion applies if we switch commitment scope from zonal to regional.

sarah: Sounds good. Can we get a rough impact estimate before we change anything? Finance please confirm expected delta if we stop replication.

finance-bot: Estimated delta for Feb (if replication stopped): -12% effective unit cost in ap-southeast1. Confidence: medium. Follow-up: manual verification required for provider tiering rules.

diego: I'll open infra-ticket INFRA-4921 to: 1) update snapshot target, 2) prototype spot-backed batch pool, 3) run perf/cost sim for 2 weeks. Assign to me + ali. ETA: EOW for prototype.

mike: Also a note for placement decisions: we should add a column in our capacity spreadsheet for "post-billing-adjusted unit cost" that includes egress, snapshot, and interconnect fees. That will make region-by-region comparisons straightforward.

sarah: +1 on the spreadsheet. Mike can you own that?

mike: Yep, I'll add it and push the link here when ready.

deploy-bot: Reminder: There's a scheduled snapshot job at 02:00 UTC Sunday for ap-southeast1 pools. Pausing or changing target will trigger a deploy job.

sarah: Thanks all — action items: Diego create ticket (INFRA-4921), Mike update cost spreadsheet + simulation numbers, Finance confirm committed SKU conversion rules and provide final delta. We'll re-evaluate placement decisions after the 2-week sim. :thumbsup:

janet: One last thing — let's capture policy: if APAC post-adjusted cost > US by X% (suggest X=5) then favor routing batch workloads to US. We'll draft policy in the ticket.

ali: I'll help verify peering/egress pricing.

sarah: Closing loop here in 2 weeks. Thanks!
